about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice C): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Asparagus and Pea Frittata Squares
recipes.summary: Fluffy baked frittata studded with spring asparagus and sweet peas, cut into squares for brunch.
steps: Heat the oven to 180C and line a 20cm square tin with baking paper.
Warm the oil in a frying pan and cook the asparagus for 3 minutes, until just tender, then stir through the peas.
Whisk the eggs with the mint, seasoning and grated cheese, then pour into the tin and scatter over the vegetables and spoonfuls of ricotta.
Bake for 22 minutes, until puffed, golden and set in the centre.
Rest for 5 minutes, then cut into 6 squares.
notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until fully set in the centre; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

recipes.title: Lemon Roasted Asparagus with Toasted Almonds
recipes.summary: Blistered asparagus finished with lemon zest and crunchy almonds, a fast spring side.
steps: Heat the oven to 220C and line a large tray with baking paper.
Toss the asparagus with half the oil and seasoning on a tray and roast for 10 minutes, until tender with charred tips.
Toast the almonds in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 3 minutes, until golden.
Stir the garlic into the remaining oil, then toss through the hot asparagus with the lemon zest and juice.
Scatter with almonds and serve warm.
notes: Serve with grilled fish or chicken.

recipes.title: Fresh Pea and Mint Soup with Lemon
recipes.summary: A bright green spring soup of sweet peas, mint and a squeeze of lemon.
steps: Warm the oil in a saucepan and cook the onion for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the potato and stock, bring to a simmer and cook for 10 minutes, until the potato is tender.
Add the peas and cook for 3 minutes, until bright green.
Blend with the mint until smooth, then stir through the lemon juice and season.
Reheat gently until steaming and serve.
notes: Swirl through a spoonful of yoghurt for extra creaminess.

recipes.title: Split Pea and Ham Soup for the Freezer
recipes.summary: A thick, comforting soup that freezes well in single portions.
steps: Warm the oil in a large pot and cook the onion, carrot and celery for 6 minutes, until soft.
Add the garlic, split peas, ham hock, bay leaves and water, stirring until it comes to the boil.
Simmer gently for 70 minutes, stirring now and then, until the peas collapse and the ham falls from the bone.
Lift out the hock, shred the meat and return it to the pot, discarding skin and bone.
Season with pepper and add a splash of water if too thick.
notes: Food safety: cool quickly, refrigerate within 2 hours and freeze in portions; reheat until steaming hot all the way through.
Freezes for up to 3 months. Taste before salting as the ham is salty.

recipes.title: Radish and Cucumber Spring Salad with Dill Yoghurt
recipes.summary: Crisp radish and cucumber ribbons tossed in a cooling dill yoghurt dressing.
steps: Whisk the yoghurt, dill, lemon juice, honey, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Add the cucumber, radish and spring onion and toss until evenly coated.
Chill for 10 minutes, until cold and crisp.
notes: Serve with rye bread or smoked fish.

recipes.title: Asparagus and New Potato Salad with Chive Vinaigrette
recipes.summary: Warm baby potatoes and asparagus in a sharp wholegrain mustard dressing.
steps: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 12 minutes, until just tender.
Add the asparagus for the final 3 minutes, until bright green and tender, then drain well.
Whisk the oil, mustard, vinegar, honey and seasoning, and toss through the warm vegetables.
Scatter with chives and serve warm or at room temperature.
notes: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

recipes.title: Pea and Feta Smash on Sourdough
recipes.summary: Smashed minty peas and salty feta piled onto crisp sourdough.
steps: Cook the peas in boiling water for 3 minutes, until tender, then drain.
Mash roughly with the oil, mint, lemon zest and pepper.
Toast the sourdough until golden and crisp.
Pile the pea smash onto the hot toast until generously covered, then top with feta.
notes: Add a poached egg for extra protein.

recipes.title: Spring Vegetable Broth with Orzo
recipes.summary: A light broth of asparagus, peas and baby zucchini with tiny orzo pasta.
steps: Warm the oil in a large saucepan and cook the leek for 5 minutes, until soft, adding the garlic for the last minute.
Add the stock and water and heat until it boils steadily.
Stir in the orzo and simmer for 8 minutes, until nearly tender.
Add the asparagus, peas and zucchini and simmer for 3 minutes, until just cooked.
Stir through the lemon zest and parsley and season.
notes: Add a squeeze of lemon at the table.

recipes.title: Low-FODMAP Friendly Chicken and Rice Soup
recipes.summary: A gentle, ginger-scented chicken soup made without onion or garlic, using garlic-infused oil.
steps: Warm the garlic-infused oil in a pot and cook the carrot, celery and ginger for 5 minutes, until softening.
Add the stock and chicken and simmer for 15 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through with no pink.
Lift out the chicken, shred it and return it to the pot with the rice.
Simmer for 12 minutes, until the rice is tender, then stir through the spinach until wilted.
Season and scatter with chives.
notes: Food safety: cook chicken until it reaches 75°C in the thickest part; refrigerate leftovers within 1 hour of cooking rice and eat within 1 day.
Check stock labels, as many contain onion and garlic.

recipes.title: Low-FODMAP Friendly Quinoa Salad with Cucumber and Olives
recipes.summary: Fluffy quinoa with cucumber, tomato, olives and feta in a lemon dressing, free of onion and garlic.
steps: Simmer the quinoa in 400ml water for 15 minutes, until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender.
Spread on a tray to cool for 10 minutes.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice and seasoning, then toss through the quinoa with the cucumber, tomato, olives and parsley, then top with the feta.
notes: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days.

recipes.title: Low-FODMAP Friendly Carrot and Ginger Soup
recipes.summary: Sweet carrot and zingy ginger blended into a velvety soup with no onion or garlic.
steps: Warm the oil in a saucepan and cook the ginger and cumin for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the carrot, potato and stock and simmer for 22 minutes, until the vegetables are very soft.
Blend until smooth and season to taste.
Reheat until steaming and scatter with chives.
notes: Freezes well for up to 3 months.

recipes.title: Low-FODMAP Friendly Tomato and Basil Soup
recipes.summary: A smooth tomato soup built on garlic-infused oil and fresh basil.
steps: Warm the oil in a saucepan and cook the carrot for 5 minutes, until softening.
Add the tomatoes, stock and sugar and simmer for 20 minutes, until the carrot is tender.
Blend with the basil until smooth.
Season and reheat until steaming.
notes: Serve with gluten-free toast if needed.

recipes.title: Low-FODMAP Friendly Spinach and Egg Breakfast Muffins
recipes.summary: Savoury egg muffins with spinach, tomato and chives that travel well.
steps: Heat the oven to 180C and oil a 6-hole muffin tin.
Whisk the eggs with the seasoning, then stir through the spinach, tomato, cheese and chives.
Divide among the holes and bake for 18 minutes, until risen and set in the centre.
Cool for 3 minutes before turning out.
notes: Food safety: cook until the eggs are fully set; refrigerate within 2 hours and eat within 2 days, reheating until steaming.

recipes.title: Low-FODMAP Friendly Greek Salad
recipes.summary: Cucumber, tomato, olives and feta with a simple lemon and oregano dressing.
steps: Combine the cucumber, tomato, capsicum and olives in a bowl.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice, oregano and seasoning and toss through the salad until coated.
Top with the feta and a pinch of oregano.
notes: Leave out the capsicum if it does not agree with you.

recipes.title: Cauliflower and Potato Smash for Fussy Eaters
recipes.summary: Creamy cauliflower mashed with a little cheese, a gentle side for fussy eaters.
steps: Boil the cauliflower and potato in salted water for 15 minutes, until very tender.
Drain well and return to the pot.
Add the butter, milk and cheese and mash until smooth and creamy.
Season to taste and serve hot.
notes: Serve with sausages or crumbed fish.

recipes.title: Kids' Hidden Veg Tomato Sauce
recipes.summary: A smooth tomato sauce with carrot, zucchini and pumpkin blended in unnoticed.
steps: Warm the oil in a large pot and cook the onion for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the carrot, zucchini and pumpkin and cook for 5 minutes, stirring until softening.
Add the tomatoes, water and oregano and simmer for 20 minutes, until the pumpkin is completely soft.
Blend until smooth and season lightly.
notes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Toss through pasta or spread on pizza bases.

recipes.title: Kids' Honey Glazed Carrot Sticks
recipes.summary: Sweet roasted carrot sticks that are easy for little hands.
steps: Heat the oven to 200C and line a large tray with baking paper.
Toss the carrots with the oil, cinnamon and a pinch of salt on a tray.
Roast for 18 minutes, until tender with golden edges.
Drizzle with the honey and roast for 2 minutes, until glossy.
notes: Not suitable for babies under 12 months because of the honey.

recipes.title: Kids' Broccoli Trees with Cheesy Dip
recipes.summary: Steamed broccoli florets with a warm cheddar dip.
steps: Steam the broccoli for 6 minutes, until bright green and just tender.
Melt the butter in a small saucepan, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Whisk in the milk gradually and stir for 4 minutes, until thickened.
Remove from the heat, stir in the cheese until melted and season with pepper.
Serve the broccoli with the dip for dunking.
notes: Let it cool a little before serving to small children.

recipes.title: Kids' Corn and Zucchini Fritters
recipes.summary: Golden little fritters packed with sweetcorn and grated zucchini.
steps: Whisk the eggs, milk and flour into a smooth batter, then fold in the zucchini, corn, chives and seasoning.
Heat half the oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
Cook spoonfuls of batter for 2 minutes each side, until golden and cooked through, working in batches with the remaining oil.
Drain on paper and serve warm.
notes: Food safety: cook until the batter is set and no longer wet in the centre.
Cooked fritters freeze well for 2 months.

recipes.title: Kids' Rainbow Veggie Rice
recipes.summary: Fluffy rice with colourful diced vegetables and a little soy sauce.
steps: Rinse the rice and place in a pot with the water and carrot.
Bring to the boil, cover and cook on low for 12 minutes, until the water is absorbed.
Stir the capsicum, peas, corn, sesame oil and soy sauce through the hot rice, cover and rest off the heat for 5 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Fluff with a fork and serve.
notes: Food safety: cool leftover rice quickly and refrigerate within 1 hour; reheat until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Kids' Mini Pea and Ham Pancakes
recipes.summary: Savoury drop pancakes with peas and diced ham for lunchboxes.
steps: Whisk the flour, baking powder, egg and milk into a smooth batter, then fold in the peas, ham and pepper.
Heat a little oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium heat.
Cook spoonfuls of batter for 2 minutes each side, until golden and cooked through.
Keep warm while cooking the rest.
notes: Food safety: cook until the batter is set; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 2 days.

recipes.title: Kids' Cucumber Boats with Hummus
recipes.summary: Cucumber halves filled with hummus and cherry tomatoes.

items: 2 Lebanese cucumbers, halved lengthways and scooped

steps: Scoop out the cucumber seeds with a teaspoon to make boats.
Spoon in the hummus until each boat is generously filled.
Top with tomato, a drizzle of oil and sesame seeds.
notes: Cut into short pieces for younger children.

recipes.title: Alphabet Pasta Chicken Soup for Kids
recipes.summary: A mild chicken soup with soft vegetables and tiny pasta letters.
steps: Warm the oil in a large pot and cook the onion, carrot and celery for 6 minutes, until soft.
Add the chicken and stock and simmer for 15 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through with no pink.
Lift out the chicken and shred it.
Add the pasta and peas and cook for 6 minutes, until the pasta is tender, then return the chicken.
Season with pepper and serve.
notes: Food safety: cook chicken until it reaches 75°C in the thickest part; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until steaming.

recipes.title: Homemade Baked Beans on Toast Fingers
recipes.summary: Smoky tomato butter beans spooned over toast fingers.

items: 2 x 400g tins butter beans, drained and rinsed

steps: Warm the oil in a saucepan and cook the onion for 5 minutes, until soft, adding the garlic for the final minute.
Stir in the paprika, tomato paste, crushed tomatoes, maple syrup and worcestershire sauce.
Add the beans and simmer for 12 minutes, until the sauce is thick.
Toast the bread until golden and cut into fingers.
Spoon the beans over the toast until generously covered.
notes: Canned beans are already cooked, so no soaking is needed.
